label: restir: HYBRID — held-light rays K (0 = off)
title: THE HYBRID ESTIMATOR: every light a character CARRIES (owner byte ≠ 0: the guards' torches, the player's rail / gun light, muzzle flashes, tracer heads) bypasses the reservoirs at the pixels it reaches and gets the old leader treatment every frame — the two strongest at the pixel take K stratified emitter samples each, shaded exactly, any further ones one tail ray a class; static lights (owner 0) keep ReSTIR. A carried light moves every frame, so its reservoir history and the shadow client's ratio history are let go wherever the cone sweeps and the pool was shaded from one or two fresh rays: noisy pools, ragged edges, rims. The presets tier K (ultra 8 · high 4 · medium 4 · low 3 · verylow 2); 0 = off, the transient stratum exactly as it was (docs/internal/direct-quality.md)

label: restir: shadow rays / pixel
title: 2 = each class alternates re-tracing its history sample and tracing a fresh candidate (flipping checkerboard) · 3 = both classes re-trace, one fresh candidate alternates · 4 = re-trace + fresh for both classes · 5 = + a final visibility ray when spatial reuse picks a neighbour's sample (spatial reuse then runs everywhere) · 6 = + a second fresh candidate per class. Presets: ultra 4 · high 4 · medium 4 · low 3 · verylow 2 (5 and 6 measured dearer than they are worth: this slider keeps them for A/B)

label: restir: spatial taps
title: neighbour reservoirs combined per pixel (pairwise MIS, plane / normal rejection) — below 5 rays only where the pixel's own history is young (see 'young M'), at 5+ everywhere with a final visibility ray. 0 = temporal reuse only. Presets 5 / 3 / 2 / 2 / 1

label: restir: history M cap
title: temporal confidence cap in candidate-equivalents: 20 ≈ a 20-frame memory where nothing changes. Big visibility / lighting changes are caught at once by the target-ratio rule and the tile gradient regardless; this sets the steady-state smoothness vs the convergence rate of SMALL changes

label: restir: spatial radius (px @1000 rows)
title: disc the spatial taps are drawn from (scaled with the internal resolution, never wider than ~0.6 m on the surface)

label: restir: tile gradient confidence
title: per 8×8 tile: the sum of this frame's fresh one-sample estimates vs the sum of the temporal ones, per class — when they disagree by more than the threshold (a shadow sweeping in or out, a door letting light in, a man stepping in front of a lamp) the tile's history confidence drops to 0 within the frame instead of the estimate converging at the M cap's rate. Off = plain capped reuse (A/B: watch the trailing edge of a walking man's shadow)

label: restir: gradient threshold z
title: the tile's paired z statistic — mean (fresh − temporal) over the lanes that have both, in units of its own sampling spread — under which the history keeps full confidence; none past 1.6× it. 5 default (3.5 until 08-11: the street lamp's patch on the floor behind the cubicles' windows — one rarely-visible light dominating the tile's weight, fat-tailed z — reset 1–2 % of its tiles a frame there and crawled): a shadow edge or a door moves dozens of lanes the same way (z ≫ 5), the steady state sits at |z| ~ 1 whatever the light level (lower = quicker but twitchier)

label: restir: young M (spatial below 5 rays)
title: without the final ray (rays < 5) a neighbour's visibility stands in for this pixel's, which softens hard shadow edges by up to the radius — so spatial reuse only runs where this pixel's history is younger than this (just disoccluded / reset: noisy anyway, and the bias lasts a few frames). 0 = never below 5 rays; 30 = always

label: restir: tile-coherent fresh draws
title: the fresh candidate (which light, which point on its emitter) comes from a random stream shared by the 8×8 tile instead of one per pixel — each pixel's draw is still distributed by its OWN weights (unbiased per pixel), but the tile ends up tracing near-parallel rays, which the GPU walks about a third cheaper; the price is one-frame sampling noise correlated in 8×8 blocks where two lights of a class cast different shadows (the history decorrelates it over frames). A/B it on penumbrae

label: restir: known-dark lights leave the draw
title: the lights an 8×8 tile's own shadow rays found dark EVERYWHERE last frame (a street lamp behind the outer wall, the next room's panel behind a shut door — in the unshadowed total, reach level > 0, never visible) leave that tile's fresh candidate draw: known dark like a reach-masked light — no ray, and none of the one-sample all-or-nothing noise that made the dim end of the break-room lino crawl (restir.wgsl BELIEFS). Off = A/B the first cut: every live light in the draw (unbiased; the auditors below then have nothing to do)

label: restir: audit fraction
title: on this share of a tile's frames (spread over every 64, staggered across tiles) EVERY lane of an 8×8 tile that holds some light dark spends one extra shadow ray re-testing one of them (drawn by unshadowed weight; the outcome only votes — whole tiles at once, because a SIMD group half-filled with audit rays pays for all of them). A light lit anywhere in the 5×5 tiles round a tile never leaves its draw, so moving shadow edges need no audit; this is what overturns a verdict for a light arriving where nothing near had it lit (a door starting to open on the next room's panel): 0 = only the reservoirs that hold a light lit can, 1 = every frame (a ray per lane per frame)

label: restir: D5 M cap inside penumbrae (0 = off)
title: the temporal confidence cap for pixels whose inherited reservoir carries a blocker-distance hint (a penumbra): shorter memory there turns the reservoir's slow random walk into per-frame noise the shadow filter and the TAA can average — the dim multi-light penumbra grain; 0 = the tier's cap everywhere

label: restir: hue split (a sample of an unbelieved light keeps its own hue)
title: the believed-visible mix colours only the luminance its own lights carried; the share of the estimate carried by a sample whose light this pixel does not believe visible (tile-dark here, or its own darkSlot) keeps that sample's hue — without it a blocked light's penumbra deep in its own shadow was painted in whatever far dim light the tile still believed: coloured fringes along shadow boundaries under two lights of different colour (docs/internal/direct-quality.md S3). Off = the belief hue as it was

label: restir: D1 second fresh ray inside penumbrae
title: a second fresh candidate + shadow ray per class in penumbra pixels whatever the tier's ray count (+1 ray where the estimate is uncertain; an auditing tile's penumbra lanes give up their audit slot that frame). On by default through the motion-calm rows

label: restir: D4 permutation sampling (whiter temporal noise)
title: each frame a pixel inherits the reservoir of a neighbour within a 2×2-ish block chosen by a per-frame XOR pattern (RTXDI's permutation sampling): the slow random walk of one reservoir per pixel becomes noise the shadow filter and the TAA can average, for a little reuse bias inside penumbrae

label: restir: A/B raw target-ratio cut (flicker drops history)
title: the temporal reservoir's confidence is cut by how much its own light's target changed at the pixel since last frame. ON = the 08-11 rule, the RAW ratio: a light that merely dimmed or brightened (the cubicles' flickering tube goes 15 % ↔ 100 % every other frame, a restrike, the lightning's decay) dropped every reservoir under it to a sample or three each stroke — 1–3-spp penumbrae the shadow filter smeared into blotches that pumped with the tube. OFF (the default) = each side of the ratio ÷ its light's power then and now: intensity / hue changes keep the visibility history (MIS weighs the two frames' targets either way), a cone that swept off the pixel or a lamp that moved still lets go (docs/internal/tjank.md)

label: restir: A/B per-sample hue (the mosaic)
title: shade every traced sample in its OWN light's colour (the estimator's first cut: unbiased per channel, but under two overlapping lights of different colours each pixel wears the colour of the light its reservoir happens to hold — a per-pixel mosaic crawling at the reservoir's rate; the break room's vending fronts show it). Off (the default) = the luminance estimate coloured by the believed-visible unshadowed mix at the pixel: per-tile lit / dark verdicts from the tile's own rays plus the pixel's own dark memory (restir.wgsl BELIEFS)

label: restir: spatial everywhere (biased)
title: spatial reuse at every pixel even without the final visibility ray: contact shadows soften by up to the radius. ON by default through Frame ▸ Quality & resolution ▸ motion-calm rows; off = only where the visibility ray runs

label: restir: motion — stochastic-bilinear reprojection
title: under a camera pan the temporal reservoir used to come from the NEAREST texel to the reprojected point: at 2.4 px a frame every pixel inherits from 2 px back while the picture moved 2.4, so the reservoir pattern slides across the floor the TAA holds still and neighbouring pixels share one verdict — 2–7-px blotches crawling under a panning floor. On: the texel is one of the four round the reprojected point, drawn by its bilinear weight per pixel per frame and validated by depth as ever, so a lineage follows the surface (diffusing ± ½ px) instead. Inert at rest by construction (docs/internal/direct-motion.md)

label: restir: motion — reprojection dither is GLOBAL (bijective shift)
title: how the stochastic reprojection above picks its texel: OFF = a per-pixel bilinear draw among the four round the reprojected point (lineages diffuse ± ½ px a frame; two neighbours can adopt one parent, so lineages coalesce into patches that grow with the memory); ON = one sub-pixel offset for the whole raster each frame (an R2 sequence) — a bijective shift, nothing duplicated or dropped, whose average over frames is the true flow, so the pattern stays registered to the surface within ± ½ px

label: restir: motion — motion-scaled confidence
title: the reservoir's memory (M cap) at a pixel shrinks with that pixel's own screen motion — whole under the 'full-confidence motion' below, down to the floor past 1.6 × it: a panning pixel leans on fresh candidates, whose error is white frame to frame (the ratio filter and the TAA average it), instead of on a history reprojected to the nearest texel from somewhere else; the full memory the moment it rests. Measured at high: a 0.8-px-a-frame pan keeps ReSTIR's history worth all 20 candidates (any cut costs 10–25 % more flow), a 1.4–2-px walking pan about two (docs/internal/direct-motion.md)

label: restir: motion — full-confidence motion (px @1000 rows)
title: screen motion per frame, in px at 1000 internal rows (scaled to the target), under which a pixel's reservoir keeps its whole memory; the cut ramps to the floor by 1.6 × this (1.1: high's walking pan of ~2 px sits past the ramp, a slow creep of 0.8 px before it)

label: restir: motion — confidence floor
title: the least fraction of the M cap a fast-moving pixel keeps (0.1 = a 2-candidate memory at cap 20)

label: restir: motion — spatial reuse under motion
title: the spatial taps run at every pixel moving faster than the threshold below (spatial-everywhere only where the history is being handed about anyway; nothing extra at rest — moot while 'A/B spatial everywhere' is on)

label: restir: motion — spatial threshold (px @1000 rows)
title: screen motion per frame, in px at 1000 internal rows (scaled to the target), past which the spatial pass opens at the pixel with the tap count below

label: restir: motion — run under a still camera too

label: trace grid: skip empty runs (lossless, all rays)
title: every traced ray (shadow rays here, the final gather, cascade intervals, beams, probes) walks the 1 m XZ grid cell by cell; the grid build stores each cell's Chebyshev distance to the nearest occupied cell, so an empty cell at distance d lets the DDA take its next d−1 steps without loading anything (those cells are provably empty too). Same stepping arithmetic, one iteration per cell as before, so hits are bit-identical — off = a load pair per cell (A/B, frame flag 131072)

label: trace grid: height cull (lossless, all rays)
title: the grid is 2D but the level is not: each cell also stores which 15 cm height slices its boxes occupy and each item its own padded [ymin, ymax]. A cell (or a single box) whose band the REST of the ray — from where it enters the cell to tmax / the current hit — cannot reach is not slab-tested: such a box could only have been hit behind the cell, where the walk already met it, so every dropped test was a miss or a no-op and the result is bit-identical (argument above traceClosest in common.wgsl). Rays skimming over desks toward ceiling panels, cascade intervals at chest height, gather rays under the furniture stop paying for geometry above/below them — off = every registered box tested (A/B, frame flag 262144)

label: slab test: unrotated fast path (lossless, all rays)
title: a box with yaw 0 packs its rotation as exactly (cos 1, sin 0), and rotating by that is the identity down to the last bit (1·x − 0·z = x however the compiler contracts it), so the ray/box test can use the ray as it is and the inverse direction the traversal already holds instead of two half-float unpacks, two rotations and three divisions — that is two thirds of all grid items and every global. Off = always rotate + divide (A/B, frame flag 524288)

label: trace grid: globals by segment + tight spans (lossless, all rays)
title: the handful of huge slabs kept out of the grid (ground, carpet base, corridor / break-room finishes, ceiling) used to be slab-tested by every ray whose HEIGHTS came within 4 cm of theirs — so a ray lifted 1–2 cm off the floor tested all four floors, four of its ~ten box tests. Now a global is skipped unless the ray segment's bounds meet its own on all three axes, 5 mm proud; and each cell's height span is judged 3.5 cm tighter at both ends (the packed extents carry 4 cm against < 0.4 mm of float differences), so a ray stops re-testing the desk / floor / wall top it just left. Every dropped test was a provable miss, so hits are bit-identical (argument above traceClosest in common.wgsl; tools/qa/grid-globals.ts: −40 % slab tests for rays off the floor, −60 % outdoors, −19 % cascades) — off = the height cull as it was (A/B, frame flag 1048576)
